meaning: no wonder; that's why; it follows that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + という + わけだ
usage: States a conclusion that follows naturally from known facts, often with a feeling of 'now I understand'. Often preceded by だから, それで or どうりで.

examples.japanese: 三年も中国に住んでいたんですか。だから中国語が上手なわけですね。
examples.english: You lived in China for three years? That's why your Chinese is so good.

examples.japanese: 窓が全部開いている。どうりで寒いわけだ。
examples.english: All the windows are open. No wonder it's cold.

examples.japanese: この本は三百ページだから、一日に二十ページ読めば、十五日で読み終わるわけだ。
examples.english: This book has 300 pages, so if I read twenty pages a day, that means I'll finish it in fifteen days.

meaning: it doesn't mean that; it's not that; not necessarily
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + という + わけではない
usage: A partial or soft denial of what the listener might assume. Often with いつも, 全部 or 必ずしも. Not the same as 〜わけがない, which flatly rules something out.

examples.japanese: 料理が嫌いなわけではないが、毎日作る時間がない。
examples.english: It's not that I dislike cooking, but I don't have time to cook every day.

examples.japanese: 値段が高ければおいしいというわけではない。
examples.english: Just because something is expensive doesn't mean it tastes good.

examples.japanese: 全然分からないわけではありませんが、もう少しゆっくり話していただけますか。
examples.english: It's not that I don't understand at all, but could you speak a little more slowly?

meaning: there's no way that; cannot possibly
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + わけがない
usage: The speaker's strong conviction that something is impossible. Casual: 〜わけない. Close to 〜はずがない, but sounds more emotional and less based on reasoning.

examples.japanese: こんなに練習したんだから、負けるわけがない。
examples.english: We've practiced this hard, so there's no way we'll lose.

examples.japanese: あんなにまじめな人が、約束を忘れるわけがありません。
examples.english: There's no way someone that conscientious would forget a promise.

examples.japanese: 一日で漢字を百個覚えるなんて、できるわけがないよ。
examples.english: Learn a hundred kanji in one day? There's no way you can do that.

meaning: can't afford to; can't very well; must not (for social or moral reasons)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + わけにはいかない
usage: The action is physically possible but ruled out by duty, circumstances or common sense. 〜ないわけにはいかない means 'have to; can't avoid doing'.

examples.japanese: 明日は大事な会議があるから、休むわけにはいかない。
examples.english: There's an important meeting tomorrow, so I can't afford to take the day off.

examples.japanese: 友達に頼まれたことだから、断るわけにはいかなかった。
examples.english: It was a favor my friend had asked, so I couldn't very well say no.

examples.japanese: 招待されたのだから、パーティーに行かないわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I was invited, so I can't not go to the party.

meaning: it's natural that; one should; used to (nostalgia); how ...! (deep feeling)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + ものだ
usage: Main uses: general truth or natural tendency, a social norm (should), a nostalgic past habit with 〜たものだ, and deep feeling (時間がたつのは早いものだ). Casual: 〜もんだ.

examples.japanese: 子どものころは、この川でよく泳いだものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, I used to swim in this river a lot.

examples.japanese: 新しい環境に慣れるには、時間がかかるものだ。
examples.english: It naturally takes time to get used to a new environment.

examples.japanese: 目上の人には敬語を使うものだ。
examples.english: You're supposed to use honorific language with your superiors.

meaning: one shouldn't; it's not right to
structure: Verb-dict + ものではない
usage: Advice based on common sense or social norms, often from an older person. Casual: 〜もんじゃない. Sounds more like general wisdom than 〜べきではない.

examples.japanese: 人の失敗を笑うものではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't laugh at other people's mistakes.

examples.japanese: 出された食べ物を残すものじゃないよ。
examples.english: You shouldn't leave food that's been served to you.

examples.japanese: 夜遅くに人の家に電話をかけるものではありません。
examples.english: One shouldn't phone someone's home late at night.

meaning: because (casual excuse or self-justification)
structure: Sentence + もの / もん
usage: Sounds pouty or self-justifying; often begins with だって. もん is more colloquial. Used by children and among close friends; avoid at work.

examples.japanese: 「どうして食べないの？」「だって、ピーマン嫌いなんだもん。」
examples.english: 'Why aren't you eating?' 'Because I hate green peppers!'

examples.japanese: 一人で行けるよ。もう子どもじゃないもん。
examples.english: I can go by myself. I'm not a kid anymore!

examples.japanese: ケーキ、全部食べちゃった。だって、すごくおいしかったんだもん。
examples.english: I ate the whole cake. Well, it was just so good!

meaning: because; since (explaining or excusing a situation)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + な + ものだから / もので
usage: Explains or excuses something that wasn't fully under the speaker's control. The main clause can't be a command or request. もので is common in polite apologies.

examples.japanese: 道がすごく混んでいたものだから、約束の時間に間に合わなかった。
examples.english: The roads were really crowded, so I couldn't make it on time.

examples.japanese: すみません、急いでいたもので、書類を持ってくるのを忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I'm sorry, I was in such a hurry that I forgot to bring the documents.

examples.japanese: 初めての海外旅行だったものだから、見るものすべてが珍しかった。
examples.english: It was my first trip abroad, so everything I saw seemed new.

meaning: should; the best thing is to (advice)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことだ
usage: Personal advice from someone in a position to give it (teacher, parent, senior). Not used toward superiors. Compare 〜ものだ, which appeals to general norms.

examples.japanese: 日本語が上手になりたいなら、毎日少しずつでも話すことだ。
examples.english: If you want to get good at Japanese, you should speak it every day, even just a little.

examples.japanese: 風邪を早く治したければ、無理をしないでゆっくり休むことです。
examples.english: If you want to get over your cold quickly, the best thing is not to push yourself and to rest well.

examples.japanese: 人の話は最後までよく聞くことだ。
examples.english: You should always listen carefully to what people say, right to the end.

meaning: there's no need to; don't have to
structure: Verb-dict + ことはない
usage: Reassures or advises that something is unnecessary. Don't confuse with 〜たことはない ('have never done').

examples.japanese: 簡単な手術ですから、そんなに心配することはありませんよ。
examples.english: It's a simple operation, so there's no need to worry so much.

examples.japanese: 駅までは歩いて五分だから、タクシーを使うことはない。
examples.english: The station is a five-minute walk, so there's no need to take a taxi.

examples.japanese: 一回失敗したくらいで、あきらめることはないよ。
examples.english: There's no need to give up just because you failed once.

meaning: make it a rule to; make a point of
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことにしている
usage: A personal rule the speaker (or subject) decided on and keeps. Compare 〜ことになっている, a rule or plan set by others.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、週に三回はジムに通うことにしている。
examples.english: For my health, I make it a rule to go to the gym at least three times a week.

examples.japanese: 夜十時以降は、スマホを見ないことにしています。
examples.english: I make a point of not looking at my phone after 10 p.m.

examples.japanese: 父は、給料日には家族を外食に連れていくことにしている。
examples.english: My dad makes a point of taking the family out to eat on payday.

meaning: it has been arranged that; it's the rule that; be supposed to
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことになっている
usage: Rules, customs or plans decided by others (a company, school, society), not a personal choice. Compare 〜ことにしている.

examples.japanese: この寮では、夜十一時までに戻ることになっている。
examples.english: In this dorm, you're supposed to be back by 11 p.m.

examples.japanese: 来月から大阪の支社で働くことになっています。
examples.english: It's been arranged that I'll work at the Osaka branch from next month.

examples.japanese: 図書館の中では、飲み物を飲んではいけないことになっている。
examples.english: The rules say you can't have drinks inside the library.

meaning: must; do (written rule or instruction)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + こと
usage: Ends a sentence with こと to state a rule. Found in notices, regulations and teacher-to-student instructions. Impersonal; not used toward superiors.

examples.japanese: レポートは、来週の金曜日までに提出すること。
examples.english: Reports must be submitted by next Friday.

examples.japanese: 図書館の本に、線を引かないこと。
examples.english: Do not draw lines in library books.

examples.japanese: 試験中は、スマホの電源を切っておくこと。
examples.english: Keep your phone switched off during the exam.

meaning: tell someone to do; ask someone to do (reported command or request)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ように言う / ように頼む
usage: Reports an instruction or request indirectly. Works with other verbs too: 伝える, 注意する, お願いする. Direct-quote version: 「〜てください」と言う.

examples.japanese: 医者に、お酒を飲みすぎないように言われた。
examples.english: My doctor told me not to drink too much.

examples.japanese: 隣の部屋の人に、夜は音楽の音を小さくするように頼んだ。
examples.english: I asked the person next door to turn their music down at night.

examples.japanese: 山下さんに、明日の会議に遅れないように伝えてください。
examples.english: Please tell Ms. Yamashita not to be late for tomorrow's meeting.

meaning: try to; attempt to; be about to
structure: Verb-volitional + とする
usage: Often an attempt that fails or is interrupted. 〜ようとしない = 'won't even try' (unwillingness). Compare 〜てみる, which means actually doing something to see how it goes.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けようとしたが、鍵がかかっていて開かなかった。
examples.english: I tried to open the door, but it was locked and wouldn't open.

examples.japanese: 家を出ようとしたとき、急に雨が降り出した。
examples.english: Just as I was about to leave the house, it suddenly started to rain.

examples.japanese: 弟は何度注意しても、部屋を片付けようとしない。
examples.english: No matter how many times I tell him, my younger brother won't even try to tidy his room.

meaning: unlikely to; doesn't look like it will
structure: Verb-stem + そうにない / そうもない
usage: Negative of the appearance 〜そうだ with verbs, based on what the speaker observes. More emphatic: 〜そうにもない. With adjectives use 〜なさそうだ instead.

examples.japanese: この雨は、夕方までやみそうにない。
examples.english: This rain doesn't look like it will stop before evening.

examples.japanese: 仕事が多すぎて、今日中には終わりそうもない。
examples.english: I have way too much work; it doesn't look like I'll finish today.

examples.japanese: こんなにたくさんの料理、二人では食べきれそうにないね。
examples.english: It doesn't look like the two of us will be able to finish all this food.

meaning: keep on -ing; more and more (change in one direction)
structure: Verb-dict + 一方だ
usage: Steady change in one direction, usually (not always) for the worse. Used with verbs of change such as 増える, 減る, 上がる, 悪くなる.

examples.japanese: この町の人口は、減る一方だ。
examples.english: This town's population just keeps on shrinking.

examples.japanese: 物価は上がる一方なのに、給料は全然上がらない。
examples.english: Prices keep going up and up, yet my salary doesn't rise at all.

examples.japanese: 勉強をさぼっていたら、成績は下がる一方だった。
examples.english: Since I kept skipping my studies, my grades just kept dropping.

meaning: while; on the other hand; at the same time
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + である + 一方で
usage: Presents two sides of one thing, or two parallel activities. Compare 〜に対して, which contrasts two different subjects.

examples.japanese: インターネットは便利な一方で、危険な面もある。
examples.english: The internet is convenient, but on the other hand it has its dangers.

examples.japanese: この会社は給料が高い一方で、休みがとても少ない。
examples.english: This company pays well, but on the other hand there are very few days off.

examples.japanese: 彼女は会社で働く一方で、夜は大学院に通っている。
examples.english: While working at a company, she also attends graduate school in the evenings.

meaning: toward; against; in contrast to
structure: Noun + に対して / Noun + に対する + Noun / Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + のに対して
usage: Marks the target of an action, attitude or feeling, or contrasts two things. Compare 〜について, which marks the topic being discussed rather than a target.

examples.japanese: お客様に対して、そんな言い方をしてはいけない。
examples.english: You mustn't speak like that to a customer.

examples.japanese: 新しい税金に対する反対の声が高まっている。
examples.english: Opposition to the new tax is growing.

examples.japanese: 東京は晴れているのに対して、大阪は朝から大雨だ。
examples.english: Whereas it's sunny in Tokyo, it's been pouring in Osaka since morning.

meaning: about; concerning; regarding
structure: Noun + について / Noun + についての + Noun
usage: Marks the topic of speaking, thinking or research. More formal: 〜に関して. Compare 〜に対して (the target of an attitude or action).

examples.japanese: 今日の授業では、日本の食文化について話し合いました。
examples.english: In today's class, we discussed Japanese food culture.

examples.japanese: 新しい商品についての質問は、こちらのメールアドレスまでお送りください。
examples.english: Please send any questions about the new product to this email address.

examples.japanese: その事件について、警察はまだ何も発表していない。
examples.english: The police haven't announced anything about the incident yet.

meaning: by (agent); by means of; due to; depending on
structure: Noun + によって / Noun + による + Noun
usage: Uses: agent of a passive (formal, for creating or discovering), cause, means, and 'varies by'. 〜によっては = 'in some cases, depending on'.

examples.japanese: この橋は、有名な建築家によって設計された。
examples.english: This bridge was designed by a famous architect.

examples.japanese: 台風による被害は、まだ正確には分かっていない。
examples.english: The full extent of the damage caused by the typhoon is still unknown.

examples.japanese: 国によって、食事のマナーはずいぶん違う。
examples.english: Table manners differ quite a lot from country to country.

meaning: according to
structure: Noun + によると / Noun + によれば
usage: Names the source of information. The sentence usually ends in a hearsay expression such as 〜そうだ, 〜らしい or 〜ということだ.

examples.japanese: 天気予報によると、週末は大雪になるそうだ。
examples.english: According to the weather forecast, there's going to be heavy snow this weekend.

examples.japanese: ニュースによれば、事故の原因はまだ分かっていないらしい。
examples.english: According to the news, the cause of the accident still isn't known.

examples.japanese: 姉の話によると、あのレストランは予約がないと入れないということだ。
examples.english: According to my sister, you can't get into that restaurant without a reservation.

meaning: not only ... but also
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + ばかりでなく
usage: Same meaning as 〜だけでなく but a little more formal. The second part usually contains も or まで.

examples.japanese: この映画は子どもばかりでなく、大人も楽しめる。
examples.english: Not only children but adults too can enjoy this film.

examples.japanese: 新しいスマホは画面が大きいばかりでなく、電池も長持ちする。
examples.english: The new smartphone not only has a big screen, its battery lasts a long time too.

examples.japanese: 運動は体にいいばかりでなく、ストレスを減らす効果もある。
examples.english: Exercise is not only good for your body, it also helps reduce stress.

meaning: not only ... but also
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + だけでなく
usage: Common in both speech and writing. Casual: 〜だけじゃなくて. Slightly less formal than 〜ばかりでなく.

examples.japanese: この店は料理がおいしいだけでなく、値段も安い。
examples.english: This restaurant not only has delicious food, it's cheap too.

examples.japanese: 地震の後、水だけでなく電気も止まってしまった。
examples.english: After the earthquake, not only the water but also the electricity was cut off.

examples.japanese: 彼女は歌が上手なだけでなく、自分で曲も作っている。
examples.english: She not only sings well but also writes her own songs.

meaning: both ... and ...; not only ... but also
structure: Noun + も + Verb-ba + Noun + も / Noun + も + i-Adj stem + ければ + Noun + も
usage: Lists two facts of the same kind for emphasis; contrasting pairs (いいときも悪いときも) are very common. Compare 〜し, which lists reasons.

examples.japanese: 彼女は歌も歌えば、ピアノも弾く。
examples.english: She both sings and plays the piano.

examples.japanese: この町には、海もあれば山もある。
examples.english: This town has both the sea and the mountains.

examples.japanese: 人生には、いいときもあれば悪いときもある。
examples.english: In life there are good times and there are bad times.

meaning: typical of; befitting; truly like
structure: Noun + らしい
usage: Having the qualities you expect of the noun. Negative: 〜らしくない ('not like'). Differs from the hearsay 〜らしい (N4) and from 〜っぽい (looks like X but isn't).

examples.japanese: 今日は春らしい暖かい一日だった。
examples.english: Today was a warm, truly spring-like day.

examples.japanese: 文句ばかり言うなんて、君らしくないね。
examples.english: Complaining all the time isn't like you.

examples.japanese: もっと学生らしい服装で来てください。
examples.english: Please come dressed in a way more appropriate for a student.

meaning: -ish; -like; tends to (casual)
structure: Noun / Verb-stem / i-Adj stem + っぽい
usage: Noun + っぽい: seems like X though it isn't (大人っぽい). Verb-stem + っぽい: tends to (怒りっぽい). Compare 〜らしい, which means truly typical of X.

examples.japanese: この服はちょっと子どもっぽいから、別のにしよう。
examples.english: This outfit is a bit childish, so let's go with a different one.

examples.japanese: 最近忘れっぽくなって、困っている。
examples.english: I've become forgetful lately, and it's a problem.

examples.japanese: あの白っぽいビルが、新しい市役所です。
examples.english: That whitish building is the new city hall.

meaning: -ic; -al; in terms of
structure: Noun + 的な + Noun / Noun + 的に
usage: Turns a (usually kanji) noun into a na-adjective: 的な before nouns, 的に before verbs and adjectives. Many are best learned as words: 具体的, 基本的, 積極的.

examples.japanese: 日本の伝統的な料理を食べてみたい。
examples.english: I'd like to try traditional Japanese food.

examples.japanese: この問題は、経済的な理由で解決が難しい。
examples.english: This problem is hard to solve for economic reasons.

examples.japanese: 個人的には、この案に賛成です。
examples.english: Personally, I'm in favor of this plan.

meaning: like; as; such as
structure: Verb-plain / Noun + の + ような / ように
usage: ような comes before nouns, ように before verbs and adjectives. AのようなB can also mean 'B such as A'. Casual: 〜みたいな / 〜みたいに.

examples.japanese: 私も、あなたのような優しい看護師になりたいです。
examples.english: I want to become a kind nurse like you, too.

examples.japanese: 先生が言ったように、この文法はテストによく出る。
examples.english: As the teacher said, this grammar point often comes up on tests.

examples.japanese: 東京のような大きな都市では、家賃がとても高い。
examples.english: In big cities such as Tokyo, rent is very high.

meaning: just like; as if
structure: まるで + Verb-plain / Noun + の + ようだ
usage: まるで signals a figurative comparison: it only seems so. Casual: まるで〜みたいだ. Compare N2 〜かのようだ.

examples.japanese: この部屋は広くて明るくて、まるでホテルのようだ。
examples.english: This room is so big and bright, it's just like a hotel.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに会った友達は、まるで別人のように変わっていた。
examples.english: My friend, whom I hadn't seen in ages, had changed so much she seemed like a different person.

examples.japanese: 三月なのに、今日はまるで真夏のように暑い。
examples.english: It's only March, but today it's as hot as midsummer.

meaning: must be; surely; no doubt
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + に違いない
usage: Strong conviction based on evidence or intuition; a slightly written tone. Compare 〜に決まっている, which is more subjective and conversational.

examples.japanese: 隣の家は何日も電気が消えている。家族で旅行に出かけたに違いない。
examples.english: The lights next door have been off for days. The family must have gone on a trip.

examples.japanese: こんなに人が並んでいるんだから、この店のラーメンはおいしいに違いない。
examples.english: With this many people in line, the ramen here must be good.

examples.japanese: この手紙の字は、父の字に違いない。
examples.english: The handwriting on this letter is surely my father's.

meaning: certainly; is bound to; of course
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + に決まっている
usage: A very confident, subjective judgment, common in conversation (〜に決まってる). More assertive than 〜に違いない and not suited to formal writing.

examples.japanese: 練習もしないで試合に出たら、負けるに決まっている。
examples.english: If you play the match without practicing, you're bound to lose.

examples.japanese: 一人で富士山に登るなんて、お母さんが心配するに決まってるでしょう。
examples.english: Climbing Mt. Fuji alone? Of course your mother's going to worry.

examples.japanese: そんなうまい話、うそに決まっているよ。
examples.english: A deal that good? It's got to be a lie.

meaning: have a feeling that; feel like
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + 気がする / Verb-plain / Noun + の + ような + 気がする
usage: A vague, intuitive impression rather than a firm judgment; ような気がする is even softer. Different from N4 〜がする (a smell, sound or taste).

examples.japanese: この人とは、どこかで会ったことがある気がする。
examples.english: I feel like I've met this person somewhere before.

examples.japanese: 今日は何か、いいことがありそうな気がする。
examples.english: I have a feeling something good is going to happen today.

examples.japanese: ドアの鍵をかけ忘れたような気がして、家に戻った。
examples.english: I had a feeling I'd forgotten to lock the door, so I went back home.

meaning: without doing
structure: Verb-nai stem + ずに
usage: More formal, written-style equivalent of 〜ないで. Irregular: する → せずに (not しずに), 来る → 来ずに (こずに).

examples.japanese: けさは朝ご飯を食べずに家を出た。
examples.english: This morning I left home without eating breakfast.

examples.japanese: 辞書を使わずに、この新聞記事が読めますか。
examples.english: Can you read this newspaper article without using a dictionary?

examples.japanese: 彼は誰にも相談せずに、会社を辞めてしまった。
examples.english: He quit the company without consulting anyone.

meaning: as it is; unchanged; while still (in a state)
structure: Verb-ta / Verb-nai / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + まま
usage: An expected change hasn't happened and the state continues. Often suggests something unusual or undesirable (leaving the lights on, shoes on indoors).

examples.japanese: エアコンをつけたまま寝てしまい、風邪をひいた。
examples.english: I fell asleep with the air conditioner on and caught a cold.

examples.japanese: この町は、私が子どもだったころのままだ。
examples.english: This town is just as it was when I was a child.

examples.japanese: 靴のまま部屋に入らないでください。
examples.english: Please don't come into the room with your shoes on.

meaning: while (before it changes); before it's too late; in the course of
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-nai / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + うちに
usage: Do something while a condition lasts, before it changes; or a change that happens unnoticed during an activity. Compare 〜間に, which marks a fixed period without that urgency.

examples.japanese: 若いうちに、いろいろな国を旅行したほうがいい。
examples.english: You should travel to lots of countries while you're young.

examples.japanese: スープが冷めないうちに、どうぞ召し上がってください。
examples.english: Please have your soup before it gets cold.

examples.japanese: 音楽を聞いているうちに、いつの間にか眠ってしまった。
examples.english: While I was listening to music, I fell asleep before I knew it.

pattern: 〜ところに / 〜ところへ / 〜ところを
meaning: just when; at the moment (someone arrives or something interrupts)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-ta + ところに / ところへ / ところを
usage: ところに/へ: something happens or someone arrives at that moment, often interrupting. ところを: the scene is the object of a verb like 見る, 見つかる, 助ける. Set phrase: お忙しいところを.

examples.japanese: 出かけようとしているところに、友達から電話がかかってきた。
examples.english: Just as I was about to go out, a friend called.

examples.japanese: みんなで君の話をしているところへ、ちょうど君が来た。
examples.english: Just as we were all talking about you, you showed up.

examples.japanese: 授業中にスマホを見ているところを、先生に見られてしまった。
examples.english: The teacher caught me looking at my phone during class.

meaning: the more ... the more
structure: Verb-ba + Verb-dict + ほど / i-Adj stem + ければ + i-Adj + ほど / na-Adj + なら + na-Adj + な + ほど
usage: The same word is repeated, first in the ば/なら form, then in plain form. The first part can be dropped: 考えるほど分からなくなる.

examples.japanese: 日本語は、勉強すればするほど面白くなる。
examples.english: The more you study Japanese, the more interesting it gets.

examples.japanese: スマホの画面は大きければ大きいほど見やすいが、持ち歩くのは大変だ。
examples.english: The bigger a phone screen, the easier it is to see, but it's a pain to carry around.

examples.japanese: 部屋が静かなら静かなほど、よく眠れる。
examples.english: The quieter the room, the better I sleep.

meaning: to the extent that; so ... that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + ほど
usage: Shows degree with an example or comparison. Often interchangeable with 〜くらい, but ほど sounds more formal and suits high degrees; it can't mark something as minimal.

examples.japanese: 昨日は、立っていられないほど疲れていた。
examples.english: Yesterday I was so tired I could hardly stand.

examples.japanese: 試験に合格したと聞いて、涙が出るほどうれしかった。
examples.english: When I heard I'd passed the exam, I was so happy I cried.

examples.japanese: このあたりは、夜になると怖いほど静かだ。
examples.english: At night this area gets so quiet it's scary.

meaning: to the extent that; so ... that; at least (something minimal)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + くらい
usage: Like 〜ほど, shows degree. くらい can also mark something as small or easy ('at least; such a simple thing as'), a use ほど doesn't have.

examples.japanese: おなかが痛くて、歩けないくらいだった。
examples.english: My stomach hurt so much I could barely walk.

examples.japanese: 隣の部屋の音楽がうるさくて、自分の声も聞こえないぐらいだ。
examples.english: The music next door is so loud I can't even hear my own voice.

examples.japanese: 自分の部屋ぐらい、自分で掃除しなさい。
examples.english: At least clean your own room yourself.

meaning: even
structure: Noun + さえ / Noun + でさえ / Noun + にさえ
usage: Gives an extreme example, implying 'so naturally the others too'. More formal than 〜も or 〜でも in this sense. As a subject: 〜でさえ. Compare N1 〜すら.

examples.japanese: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べる時間さえなかった。
examples.english: I was so busy I didn't even have time to eat lunch.

examples.japanese: こんな簡単な問題は、小学生でさえ解ける。
examples.english: Even an elementary school student could solve such an easy problem.

examples.japanese: 彼女は親友にさえ本当のことを話さなかった。
examples.english: She didn't tell the truth even to her best friend.

meaning: if only; as long as; provided that
structure: Noun + さえ + Verb-ba / Verb-stem + さえ + すれば / Verb-te + さえ + いれば
usage: Stresses that this one condition is enough by itself, or is the only thing missing.

examples.japanese: このアプリさえあれば、どこでも日本語の勉強ができる。
examples.english: As long as you have this app, you can study Japanese anywhere.

examples.japanese: 時間さえあれば、もっと旅行に行きたいんですが。
examples.english: If only I had the time, I'd love to travel more.

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んで寝てさえいれば、すぐに治りますよ。
examples.english: As long as you take your medicine and stay in bed, you'll be better in no time.

meaning: precisely; it is ... that; (strong emphasis)
structure: Noun + こそ
usage: Singles out one thing as the very one that matters. こちらこそ is a set reply: 'the thanks/pleasure is mine'. Related N2 forms: 〜からこそ, 〜てこそ.

examples.japanese: 「いつもありがとう。」「いえ、こちらこそ。」
examples.english: 'Thanks for everything.' 'No, thank you!'

examples.japanese: 今年こそ、たばこをやめるつもりだ。
examples.english: This year, for sure, I'm going to quit smoking.

examples.japanese: 毎日の小さな努力こそが、大きな成功につながる。
examples.english: It's precisely small daily efforts that lead to great success.

meaning: as; in the role or capacity of
structure: Noun + として / Noun + としての + Noun
usage: States a role, status or category. Compare 〜にとって, which states from whose point of view a judgment is made.

examples.japanese: 兄は、エンジニアとしてアメリカの会社で働いている。
examples.english: My older brother works as an engineer at an American company.

examples.japanese: この町は、温泉地として有名です。
examples.english: This town is famous as a hot-spring resort.

examples.japanese: 社会人としての責任を持って行動してください。
examples.english: Please act with the responsibility expected of a working adult.

meaning: for; to (from the standpoint of)
structure: Noun + にとって / Noun + にとっての + Noun
usage: Followed by an evaluation (大切だ, 難しい, 便利だ). Not for actions or attitudes toward someone; use 〜に対して for those.

examples.japanese: 私にとって、家族は何よりも大切なものです。
examples.english: To me, family is more important than anything.

examples.japanese: このあたりの坂道は、お年寄りにとってはかなり大変だ。
examples.english: The slopes around here are quite tough for elderly people.

examples.japanese: 留学は、彼にとっていい経験になったようだ。
examples.english: Studying abroad seems to have been a good experience for him.

meaning: for (considering it's); unexpectedly for
structure: Verb-plain / Noun + にしては
usage: The result is different from what you'd expect of X. Doesn't follow adjectives; compare 〜わりに, which can and focuses on degree (price, age, effort).

examples.japanese: 初めて作ったにしては、このケーキはよくできている。
examples.english: For a first attempt, this cake turned out really well.

examples.japanese: 彼は小学生にしては、ずいぶん難しい言葉を知っている。
examples.english: For an elementary school kid, he knows some pretty difficult words.

examples.japanese: 十月にしては、今日はずいぶん暑いね。
examples.english: It's pretty hot today for October.

meaning: even if; even considering; granted that
structure: Verb-plain / Noun + にしても
usage: Accepts a point, then says it doesn't change the speaker's view. Often accepts a fact; compare 〜としても, which is more purely hypothetical.

examples.japanese: 忙しかったにしても、電話一本ぐらいできたでしょう。
examples.english: Even if you were busy, you could at least have made one phone call.

examples.japanese: 冗談にしても、そんな言い方はひどいよ。
examples.english: Even if it was a joke, that was a terrible thing to say.

examples.japanese: 引っ越すにしても、来年の春以降になると思います。
examples.english: Even if we do move, I think it'll be after next spring.

meaning: regarding; concerning; related to
structure: Noun + に関して / Noun + に関する + Noun
usage: More formal than 〜について; common in business, news and writing. Before a noun, use に関する (or に関しての).

examples.japanese: 新しいサービスに関してご質問がある方は、受付までどうぞ。
examples.english: Anyone with questions regarding the new service, please come to the reception desk.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本の歴史に関する本をたくさん持っている。
examples.english: He owns a lot of books on Japanese history.

examples.japanese: 事故の原因に関しては、現在調査中です。
examples.english: The cause of the accident is currently under investigation.

meaning: compared to; in comparison with
structure: Noun + に比べて / Verb-dict + のに比べて
usage: Also 〜と比べて, 〜に比べると and 〜に比べれば. Sets two things side by side more explicitly than 〜より.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は、去年に比べてずいぶん涼しい。
examples.english: This summer is much cooler compared to last year.

examples.japanese: 都会に比べて、田舎は家賃が安い。
examples.english: Compared to the city, rent in the countryside is cheap.

examples.japanese: 電車で行くのに比べて、車で行くと三十分ほど長くかかる。
examples.english: Compared to going by train, driving takes about thirty minutes longer.

meaning: instead of; on behalf of; replacing
structure: Noun + に代わって / Noun + に代わり
usage: Someone acts for another person, or something new replaces something old. Written form: 〜に代わり. Compare 〜代わりに (instead of doing; in exchange for).

examples.japanese: 入院中の社長に代わって、副社長があいさつをした。
examples.english: The vice president gave the speech on behalf of the president, who is in hospital.

examples.japanese: 最近は、紙の新聞に代わって、スマホでニュースを読む人が増えている。
examples.english: More and more people these days read the news on their phones instead of in paper newspapers.

examples.japanese: 父に代わって、私が町内会の会議に出席しました。
examples.english: I attended the neighborhood association meeting in place of my father.

meaning: instead of; in exchange for; to make up for
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + 代わりに
usage: Three uses: substitution (instead of), exchange (in return for), and compensation (a downside balanced by an upside).

examples.japanese: 今日は外で食べる代わりに、家でカレーを作った。
examples.english: Instead of eating out today, I made curry at home.

examples.japanese: 友達に英語を教える代わりに、ギターを教えてもらっている。
examples.english: In exchange for teaching my friend English, I'm getting guitar lessons.

examples.japanese: このアパートは駅から遠い代わりに、家賃が安い。
examples.english: This apartment is far from the station, but to make up for it, the rent is cheap.

meaning: in accordance with; following; as ... (so ...)
structure: Noun + に従って / Verb-dict + に従って
usage: With nouns such as rules or instructions: 'following, obeying'. With Verb-dict: proportional change like 〜につれて, in a more formal tone.

examples.japanese: 係の人の指示に従って、落ち着いて避難してください。
examples.english: Please evacuate calmly, following the staff's instructions.

examples.japanese: 高く登るに従って、気温が下がっていった。
examples.english: The higher we climbed, the lower the temperature dropped.

examples.japanese: 町が大きくなるに従って、交通の問題も増えてきた。
examples.english: As the town grew, traffic problems increased too.

meaning: as (one thing changes, another changes too)
structure: Verb-dict / Noun + につれて
usage: Both halves describe gradual change. The main clause can't be a request or the speaker's intention. Close to 〜に従って and 〜とともに.

examples.japanese: 年をとるにつれて、朝早く目が覚めるようになった。
examples.english: As I've gotten older, I've started waking up early in the morning.

examples.japanese: 日本での生活に慣れるにつれて、友達も増えていった。
examples.english: As I got used to life in Japan, I made more and more friends.

examples.japanese: 時間がたつにつれて、その事故のことは忘れられていった。
examples.english: As time passed, the accident was gradually forgotten.

meaning: together with; along with; as; at the same time as
structure: Noun + とともに / Verb-dict + とともに
usage: Formal version of 〜と一緒に. Also marks events happening at the same moment, or proportional change like 〜につれて.

examples.japanese: 社長は、社員とともに新しい工場の完成を喜んだ。
examples.english: The company president celebrated the completion of the new factory together with the staff.

examples.japanese: 経済の発展とともに、人々の生活も大きく変わった。
examples.english: Along with economic development, people's lives changed greatly too.

examples.japanese: ベルが鳴るとともに、学生たちは教室を飛び出した。
examples.english: The moment the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.

meaning: every time; whenever
structure: Verb-dict / Noun + の + たびに
usage: Each time A happens, B happens too. More emphatic than 〜と or 〜ときはいつも.

examples.japanese: この写真を見るたびに、大学時代を思い出す。
examples.english: Every time I look at this photo, I remember my university days.

examples.japanese: 姉は出張のたびに、お土産を買ってきてくれる。
examples.english: My older sister brings me a souvenir every time she goes on a business trip.

examples.japanese: この川は、大雨が降るたびにあふれて、道が通れなくなる。
examples.english: Every time there's heavy rain, this river overflows and the road becomes impassable.

meaning: every; each; at intervals of
structure: Noun + ごとに / Verb-dict + ごとに
usage: Regular repetition, or each unit in turn. With Verb-dict it's close to 〜たびに. Careful: 一日ごとに = every day, but 一日おきに (N4) = every other day.

examples.japanese: このバスは十五分ごとに出ています。
examples.english: This bus leaves every fifteen minutes.

examples.japanese: 季節ごとに、店の飾りが変わる。
examples.english: The shop's decorations change with each season.

examples.japanese: 一回使うごとにポイントがたまるカードです。
examples.english: It's a card that earns you points every time you use it.

meaning: right in the middle of; while (busy with)
structure: Verb-te + いる / Noun + の + 最中に
usage: Stresses the height of an activity, usually when something unexpected interrupts it. Stronger than 〜中に or 〜ている間に. Also 〜最中だ.

examples.japanese: 大事な会議の最中に、携帯電話が鳴ってしまった。
examples.english: My cell phone went off right in the middle of an important meeting.

examples.japanese: 料理をしている最中に、停電になった。
examples.english: The power went out right in the middle of my cooking.

examples.japanese: 今、試験の最中だから、廊下では静かにしてください。
examples.english: An exam is in progress right now, so please be quiet in the hallway.

meaning: while (at it); on the occasion of; since one is doing it anyway
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / Noun + の + ついでに
usage: The main action happens anyway; the second is added because it's convenient. Compare N1 〜がてら.

examples.japanese: 郵便局へ行くついでに、この手紙も出してきてくれる？
examples.english: Since you're going to the post office, could you mail this letter too?

examples.japanese: 京都へ出張したついでに、昔の友達に会ってきた。
examples.english: While I was on a business trip to Kyoto, I took the chance to see an old friend.

examples.japanese: 買い物のついでに、図書館に本を返した。
examples.english: I returned some books to the library while I was out shopping.

meaning: thanks to; because of (good result)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + おかげで
usage: Cause of a good result, with a feeling of gratitude. Sometimes used sarcastically for a bad result (君のおかげで遅刻したよ). Compare 〜せいで (blame).

examples.japanese: 先輩が手伝ってくれたおかげで、仕事が早く終わった。
examples.english: Thanks to my senior colleague's help, the work was finished early.

examples.japanese: 薬が効いたおかげで、熱が下がった。
examples.english: Thanks to the medicine, my fever went down.

examples.japanese: 駅が近いおかげで、雨の日も楽に通勤できる。
examples.english: Because the station is close by, commuting is easy even on rainy days.

meaning: because of; due to (bad result, blame)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + せいで
usage: Cause of a bad result, placing blame. 〜のせいにする = 'blame something on'. The opposite feeling of 〜おかげで.

examples.japanese: 電車が遅れたせいで、面接に遅刻してしまった。
examples.english: Because the train was delayed, I was late for my interview.

examples.japanese: 夜中に犬がうるさかったせいで、ほとんど眠れなかった。
examples.english: Because the dog was so noisy in the middle of the night, I could barely sleep.

examples.japanese: 私が道を間違えたせいで、みんなを待たせてしまった。
examples.english: Because I took a wrong turn, I kept everyone waiting.

meaning: the moment; just as (something unexpected happens)
structure: Verb-ta + とたん / とたんに
usage: The second event is sudden and outside the speaker's control. Not used for the speaker's own planned actions, requests or intentions.

examples.japanese: 立ち上がったとたんに、めまいがした。
examples.english: The moment I stood up, I felt dizzy.

examples.japanese: 家を出たとたん、雨が降り出した。
examples.english: Just as I stepped out of the house, it started to rain.

examples.japanese: その歌手がステージに現れたとたん、会場から大きな拍手が起こった。
examples.english: The moment the singer appeared on stage, the audience burst into applause.

meaning: when I did A, (I found that) B; upon doing, I discovered
structure: Verb-ta + ら ... Verb-ta
usage: After an action, the speaker notices or discovers something. The second clause is past and outside the speaker's control. 〜と〜た is a more written equivalent.

examples.japanese: 窓を開けたら、外は一面の雪だった。
examples.english: When I opened the window, everything outside was covered in snow.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに実家に帰ったら、近所に大きなマンションが建っていた。
examples.english: When I went back to my parents' place for the first time in ages, I found a big apartment building had gone up nearby.

examples.japanese: かばんの中を探してみたら、なくしたと思っていた鍵が出てきた。
examples.english: When I searched my bag, the key I thought I'd lost turned up.

meaning: even if; no matter (casual)
structure: Verb-ta + って / i-Adj-ku + たって / na-Adj / Noun + だって
usage: Colloquial form of 〜ても / 〜でも, often with いくら or question words. だって also means 'because' at the start of a sentence, and 'even' after nouns.

examples.japanese: 今から急いだって、もう間に合わないよ。
examples.english: Even if you hurry now, you won't make it.

examples.japanese: 高くたって、欲しいものは欲しい。
examples.english: Even if it's expensive, I want what I want.

examples.japanese: いくら便利だって、使い方が分からなければ意味がない。
examples.english: No matter how convenient it is, it's pointless if you don't know how to use it.

meaning: it's not that ... not; can if necessary; not impossible
structure: Verb-nai / i-Adj-ku + ない / na-Adj + でない + ことはない
usage: A double negative giving a hesitant 'yes'. Also 〜ないこともない. Don't confuse with Verb-dict + ことはない ('there's no need to').

examples.japanese: 辛い料理は食べられないことはないけど、あまり好きじゃない。
examples.english: It's not that I can't eat spicy food, but I don't really like it.

examples.japanese: 今から急げば、間に合わないことはないと思う。
examples.english: If we hurry now, I think we can just about make it.

examples.japanese: この服、少し派手だけど、似合わないことはないよ。
examples.english: This outfit is a bit flashy, but it's not as if it doesn't suit you.

pattern: 〜てしょうがない / 〜てしかたがない
meaning: extremely; can't help (feeling); unbearably
structure: Verb-te / i-Adj-ku + て / na-Adj + で + しょうがない / しかたがない
usage: For feelings and sensations the speaker can't control. しょうがない is more casual. Unlike 〜てたまらない, it also works with spontaneous verbs like 気になる or 涙が出る.

examples.japanese: 昨日あまり寝ていないので、眠くてしょうがない。
examples.english: I barely slept last night, so I'm terribly sleepy.

examples.japanese: 来週の旅行が楽しみでしかたがない。
examples.english: I'm so excited about next week's trip I can hardly wait.

examples.japanese: 一人暮らしを始めたばかりのころは、家族のことが気になってしかたがなかった。
examples.english: When I'd just started living alone, I couldn't stop worrying about my family.

meaning: unbearably; dying to; extremely (feeling)
structure: Verb-te / i-Adj-ku + て / na-Adj + で + たまらない
usage: Strong, direct feelings or bodily sensations; very common with desire (〜たくてたまらない). Not used for objective facts. Compare 〜てしかたがない.

examples.japanese: この部屋はエアコンがなくて、暑くてたまらない。
examples.english: This room has no air conditioning; it's unbearably hot.

examples.japanese: 三年ぶりに国の家族に会えるので、うれしくてたまらない。
examples.english: I'm going to see my family back home for the first time in three years, and I'm overjoyed.

examples.japanese: 試合に負けたのが悔しくてたまらなかった。
examples.english: I was terribly frustrated that we lost the match.

meaning: only after; not until
structure: Verb-te + はじめて
usage: Something is realized or becomes possible only after an experience; often followed by 分かる, 気づく or 知る. Also written 〜て初めて.

examples.japanese: 病気になってはじめて、健康のありがたさが分かった。
examples.english: It was only after I got sick that I appreciated how precious good health is.

examples.japanese: 一人で暮らしてはじめて、親の苦労が分かった。
examples.english: Only after living alone did I understand how hard my parents had worked.

examples.japanese: 実際に使ってみてはじめて、この機械の便利さに気づいた。
examples.english: It wasn't until I actually tried it that I realized how handy this machine is.

meaning: do nothing but; keep on doing (critical)
structure: Verb-te + ばかりいる
usage: A repeated or constant action, usually with criticism or dissatisfaction. Compare N4 Noun + ばかり (甘い物ばかり食べる).

examples.japanese: 弟は休みの日、ゲームをしてばかりいる。
examples.english: On his days off, my younger brother does nothing but play games.

examples.japanese: 泣いてばかりいないで、どうしたのか話してごらん。
examples.english: Stop crying and tell me what happened.

examples.japanese: 休みの間、寝てばかりいたら、かえって疲れてしまった。
examples.english: I did nothing but sleep during the break, and it actually made me more tired.

meaning: should; all you need to do is; I hope (with のに/けど: I wish)
structure: Verb-ba + いい / i-Adj stem + ければ + いい
usage: Asks for or gives advice (〜ばいいですか = 'what should I do?'). 〜ばいいのに = 'I wish'. 〜たらいい is a near-synonym; 〜ほうがいい sounds more insistent.

examples.japanese: 「この書類、どこに出せばいいですか。」「二階の受付に出してください。」
examples.english: 'Where should I hand in this form?' 'Please take it to the reception desk on the second floor.'

examples.japanese: 分からないことがあったら、遠慮しないで私に聞けばいいよ。
examples.english: If there's anything you don't understand, just ask me. Don't be shy.

examples.japanese: 明日、雨が降らなければいいんだけど。
examples.english: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.

meaning: in the case of; if; in the event that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + 場合（は）
usage: Typical of instructions, rules and announcements about possible situations. Unlike 〜たら, it is not used to narrate a one-off past event.

examples.japanese: 雨の場合は、試合は中止になります。
examples.english: In case of rain, the game will be canceled.

examples.japanese: カードをなくした場合は、すぐに銀行に連絡してください。
examples.english: If you lose your card, contact the bank immediately.

examples.japanese: 予約の時間に遅れる場合は、お電話でお知らせください。
examples.english: If you are going to be late for your appointment, please let us know by phone.

meaning: if; supposing that; assuming
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + だ / Noun + だ + とすれば / としたら
usage: Sets up a hypothesis and considers what follows. Often with もし or 仮に. としたら is more conversational; とすれば sounds more like logical reasoning.

examples.japanese: もし宝くじで一億円当たったとしたら、何に使いますか。
examples.english: If you won 100 million yen in the lottery, what would you spend it on?

examples.japanese: 今から出発するとすれば、向こうに着くのは夜の九時ごろになる。
examples.english: If we set off now, we'll get there at around nine at night.

examples.japanese: 彼の話が本当だとしたら、大変なことになる。
examples.english: If what he says is true, we're in serious trouble.

meaning: even if; even supposing
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + だ / Noun + だ + としても
usage: Hypothetical concession: even assuming A, B still holds. More hypothetical than 〜ても; compare 〜にしても, which often accepts a fact.

examples.japanese: 親に反対されたとしても、私は留学するつもりだ。
examples.english: Even if my parents are against it, I intend to study abroad.

examples.japanese: 今からタクシーに乗ったとしても、九時の飛行機には間に合わないだろう。
examples.english: Even if we took a taxi now, we probably wouldn't make the nine o'clock flight.

examples.japanese: それが本当だとしても、ほかの人に話すべきではない。
examples.english: Even if that's true, you shouldn't tell anyone else.

meaning: I heard something like; apparently
structure: Sentence + とか
usage: Vague hearsay; softer and less certain than 〜そうだ. Often 〜とかいう話だ, 〜とか聞いた, or 〜とかで (giving a reported reason). Different from listing 〜とか〜とか.

examples.japanese: 駅前の本屋、今月で閉店するとか。寂しくなりますね。
examples.english: I hear the bookstore by the station is closing at the end of this month. It'll be sad to see it go.

examples.japanese: 今年の冬は、例年より寒くなるとかいう話だよ。
examples.english: Word is that this winter is going to be colder than usual.

examples.japanese: 部長は今日、熱があるとかで休んでいます。
examples.english: The department manager is off today; something about having a fever.

meaning: (casual quotation) says that; I heard; as for; what is
structure: Sentence + って / Noun + って
usage: Casual stand-in for と (quoting), そうだ (hearsay, often 〜んだって) and は (topic, especially 'what is X?'). Common in speech; avoided in formal writing.

examples.japanese: 彼女、今日は来られないって。
examples.english: She says she can't come today.

examples.japanese: 駅前に新しいカフェができたんだって。行ってみない？
examples.english: Apparently a new café opened by the station. Want to go check it out?

examples.japanese: 「ふろしき」って何ですか。
examples.english: What's a furoshiki?

meaning: I heard that; it means that; in other words
structure: Sentence + ということだ
usage: Two uses: reporting information (more formal than 〜そうだ) and drawing a conclusion ('so that means ...'). The conclusion use often ends in ということですね.

examples.japanese: 駅員さんの話では、事故のため電車は一時間ほど止まるということです。
examples.english: According to the station attendant, trains will be stopped for about an hour because of an accident.

examples.japanese: 「申し込みは明日までです。」「じゃあ、今日中に書類を準備しなければならないということですね。」
examples.english: 'Applications close tomorrow.' 'So that means I have to get my documents ready today, right?'

examples.japanese: 全員が賛成したということは、この計画で進めてもいいということだ。
examples.english: Everyone agreeing means we can go ahead with this plan.

meaning: what is meant by ... is; ... means; the reason is
structure: Noun / Sentence + というのは
usage: Introduces a word to define or a situation to comment on. Casual: 〜って. At the start of a sentence, というのは introduces a reason ending in 〜からだ. Written: 〜とは.

examples.japanese: 「割り勘」というのは、食事代などをみんなで同じ金額ずつ払うことです。
examples.english: 'Warikan' means everyone paying the same share of a meal or other bill.

examples.japanese: 一人で海外に住むというのは、思ったより大変なことだ。
examples.english: Living abroad on your own is harder than you'd think.

examples.japanese: 来週の旅行には行けなくなった。というのは、急に出張が入ったからだ。
examples.english: I can't go on next week's trip after all. That's because a business trip suddenly came up.

meaning: rather than; not so much A as B
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + というより
usage: Corrects or refines a description: the second one fits better. Often followed by むしろ.

examples.japanese: 今日は涼しいというより、寒いくらいだ。
examples.english: Today it's not so much cool as almost cold.

examples.japanese: 彼女は友達というより、家族のような存在だ。
examples.english: She's less a friend than something like family to me.

examples.japanese: それは意見というより、ただの文句だよ。
examples.english: That's not so much an opinion as just a complaint.

meaning: considering; for (unexpectedly)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + わりに
usage: The result doesn't match the degree you'd expect from A (price, age, effort). Can follow adjectives, unlike 〜にしては.

examples.japanese: この店は値段のわりに、量が多くておいしい。
examples.english: For the price, this restaurant gives you big, tasty portions.

examples.japanese: 兄はよく食べるわりには、全然太らない。
examples.english: Considering how much he eats, my older brother never gains weight.

examples.japanese: このホテルは駅から近いわりに、静かでよく眠れた。
examples.english: Considering how close it is to the station, the hotel was quiet and I slept well.

meaning: even though; despite (critical, reproachful)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + くせに
usage: Like 〜のに, but with contempt or reproach toward the subject. Both clauses share the same subject; rarely used about oneself. Casual.

examples.japanese: 自分では何もしないくせに、人の仕事には文句ばかり言う。
examples.english: He never does anything himself, yet he's always complaining about other people's work.

examples.japanese: 知っているくせに、どうして教えてくれなかったの？
examples.english: You knew all along, so why didn't you tell me?

examples.japanese: 弟は体が大きいくせに、小さな虫をこわがる。
examples.english: My younger brother is so big, and yet he's scared of tiny bugs.

meaning: from ... through; over (a period or area)
structure: Noun + から + Noun + にかけて
usage: A rough span of time or space whose edges aren't exact; common in weather reports. Compare 〜から〜まで, which marks clear start and end points.

examples.japanese: 今夜から明日の朝にかけて、強い雨が降るでしょう。
examples.english: Heavy rain is expected from tonight through tomorrow morning.

examples.japanese: 関東から東北にかけての広い地域で、強い揺れが観測された。
examples.english: Strong shaking was recorded over a wide area from Kanto to Tohoku.

examples.japanese: この花は、三月から四月にかけてきれいに咲く。
examples.english: This flower blooms beautifully from March through April.

meaning: for the first time in (a period); manner, way of doing
structure: Noun + ぶり / Verb-stem + ぶり
usage: Time span + ぶり: the first time in that long (〜ぶりに / 〜ぶりの). Noun or Verb-stem + ぶり: the way someone does something (仕事ぶり, 話しぶり).

examples.japanese: 五年ぶりに高校の友達に会って、話が止まらなかった。
examples.english: I saw my high school friends for the first time in five years, and we couldn't stop talking.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりですね。お元気でしたか。
examples.english: It's been a long time. How have you been?

examples.japanese: 新入社員の仕事ぶりを見て、部長は安心したようだ。
examples.english: The manager seemed relieved after seeing how the new employee works.

meaning: was it?; did I?; (trying to recall)
structure: Verb-ta / Noun + だ / Noun + だった + っけ
usage: Checks something you've forgotten, or recalls the past fondly (〜たっけ). Polite forms: 〜でしたっけ, 〜ましたっけ.

examples.japanese: あれ、会議って何時からだっけ？
examples.english: Wait, what time does the meeting start again?

examples.japanese: すみません、お名前、何とおっしゃいましたっけ。
examples.english: I'm sorry, what did you say your name was?

examples.japanese: 子どものころ、よくこの公園で遊んだっけ。
examples.english: I used to play in this park a lot as a kid, didn't I.

meaning: I hope; may (wish, prayer)
structure: Verb-stem + ますように / Verb-stem + ませんように
usage: Used for wishes and prayers, e.g. at a shrine or on tanabata strips, and at the end of letters wishing someone well.

examples.japanese: 試験に合格できますように。
examples.english: I hope I pass the exam.

examples.japanese: 明日の遠足、雨が降りませんように。
examples.english: Please don't let it rain on tomorrow's school outing.

examples.japanese: 家族みんなが元気で過ごせますように。
examples.english: May everyone in my family stay healthy.

meaning: pretend to; act as if
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + ふりをする
usage: Deliberately giving a false impression. Verb-ta is common: 寝たふり, 死んだふり.

examples.japanese: 母に呼ばれたが、聞こえないふりをしてゲームを続けた。
examples.english: My mother called me, but I pretended not to hear and kept playing my game.

examples.japanese: 彼は本当は知っているのに、知らないふりをしている。
examples.english: He actually knows, but he's pretending not to.

examples.japanese: 電車の中で、寝たふりをして席を譲らない人がいる。
examples.english: Some people on the train pretend to be asleep so they don't have to give up their seats.

meaning: suitable for / aimed at; intended for
structure: Noun + 向き / Noun + 向け
usage: 向き: happens to suit X well. 向け: made on purpose for X. 向き also means 'facing' (南向きの部屋).

examples.japanese: この料理は作り方が簡単なので、初心者向きだ。
examples.english: This dish is easy to make, so it's well suited to beginners.

examples.japanese: この雑誌は、若い女性向けに作られている。
examples.english: This magazine is made for young women.

examples.japanese: 子ども向けの番組だが、大人が見ても十分楽しめる。
examples.english: It's a program aimed at children, but adults can enjoy it too.

meaning: tend to; be prone to; often
structure: Verb-stem / Noun + がち
usage: A frequent tendency toward something undesirable. Compare 〜やすい (easily happens, can be neutral) and 〜気味 (a slight sign of a condition now).

examples.japanese: 冬になると、つい家にこもりがちになる。
examples.english: When winter comes, I tend to stay cooped up at home.

examples.japanese: 娘は小さいころ病気がちだったが、今はとても元気だ。
examples.english: My daughter was often sick when she was little, but now she's very healthy.

examples.japanese: 一人暮らしだと、野菜が不足しがちです。
examples.english: When you live alone, you tend not to get enough vegetables.

meaning: a touch of; slightly; somewhat (in that condition)
structure: Noun / Verb-stem + 気味
usage: A slight sign of a (usually negative) condition at present. Compare 〜がち, which means something happens often.

examples.japanese: 少し風邪気味なので、今日は早めに帰ります。
examples.english: I have a bit of a cold, so I'll head home early today.

examples.japanese: 最近、仕事が忙しくて疲れ気味だ。
examples.english: Work has been busy lately, and I'm feeling a little worn out.

examples.japanese: 人手が足りず、工事は予定より遅れ気味だ。
examples.english: They're short-handed, so the construction is running a little behind schedule.

meaning: full of; covered with; riddled with
structure: Noun + だらけ
usage: An unpleasantly large amount of something covering or filling a place; usually negative. Compare N1 〜まみれ (covered in something sticky or dirty).

examples.japanese: 子どもたちは、泥だらけになって帰ってきた。
examples.english: The children came home covered in mud.

examples.japanese: 急いで書いたレポートは、間違いだらけだった。
examples.english: The report I wrote in a hurry was full of mistakes.

examples.japanese: 引っ越したばかりで、部屋はまだ段ボールだらけだ。
examples.english: I've just moved, so my place is still full of cardboard boxes.

meaning: do completely; finish / can't finish; too many to
structure: Verb-stem + 切る / Verb-stem + 切れない
usage: Doing something through to the very end. Also describes a total state: 疲れ切る ('be utterly exhausted'). Often written in kana: 〜きる / 〜きれない.

examples.japanese: 三時間かけて、長い小説を最後まで読み切った。
examples.english: It took three hours, but I read the long novel right to the end.

examples.japanese: 注文しすぎて、料理を食べ切れなかった。
examples.english: We ordered too much and couldn't finish all the food.

examples.japanese: 山の上では、数え切れないほどの星が見えた。
examples.english: From the mountaintop we could see more stars than we could count.

meaning: half-done; start to; be about to
structure: Verb-stem + かける / Verb-stem + かけの + Noun
usage: An action has started but isn't finished, or something is on the verge of happening (死にかける). Verb-stem + かけの + noun describes the half-finished thing.

examples.japanese: 読みかけの本が、机の上に置いてある。
examples.english: There's a half-read book on the desk.

examples.japanese: 彼女は何か言いかけたが、そのまま黙ってしまった。
examples.english: She started to say something, but then fell silent.

examples.japanese: この花は枯れかけていたが、水をやったら元気になった。
examples.english: This flower was starting to wilt, but it perked up after I watered it.

meaning: do to each other; do together
structure: Verb-stem + 合う
usage: Reciprocal or shared action. Many compounds are set words: 話し合う, 知り合う, 付き合う, 助け合う.

examples.japanese: 困ったときは、お互いに助け合いましょう。
examples.english: Let's help each other out when things get tough.

examples.japanese: 旅行の計画について、家族で話し合った。
examples.english: We talked over the travel plans as a family.

examples.japanese: 優勝が決まると、選手たちは抱き合って喜んだ。
examples.english: When their victory was confirmed, the players hugged each other in joy.

meaning: redo; do over again (to fix or improve)
structure: Verb-stem + 直す
usage: Doing something again in order to correct or improve it. Plain repetition (もう一度〜する) doesn't carry that sense of fixing.

examples.japanese: 名前を間違えたので、書類を書き直した。
examples.english: I got the name wrong, so I rewrote the document.

examples.japanese: すみません、電波が悪いので、あとでかけ直します。
examples.english: Sorry, the signal's bad, so I'll call you back later.

examples.japanese: 一度はあきらめた夢だが、もう一度考え直してみることにした。
examples.english: It's a dream I once gave up on, but I've decided to reconsider it.

meaning: hard to; difficult or uncomfortable to
structure: Verb-stem + づらい
usage: Stresses the doer's physical or psychological discomfort. 〜にくい (N4) is more objective, describing a thing's nature. Formal N2: 〜がたい.

examples.japanese: この靴は少し小さくて、歩きづらい。
examples.english: These shoes are a bit small, so they're hard to walk in.

examples.japanese: 先輩にお金を貸してほしいとは、ちょっと言いづらい。
examples.english: It's a bit awkward to ask a senior colleague to lend me money.

examples.japanese: 字が小さくて読みづらいので、もう少し大きくしてもらえますか。
examples.english: The text is too small to read comfortably. Could you make it a bit bigger?

meaning: should; ought to / should not
structure: Verb-dict + べきだ / Verb-dict + べきではない
usage: A strong opinion about what is right or one's duty; too blunt to use toward superiors. する → すべき or するべき. Compare 〜ほうがいい (advice) and 〜ものだ (social norm).

examples.japanese: 自分が悪いと思ったら、すぐに謝るべきだ。
examples.english: If you think you were in the wrong, you should apologize right away.

examples.japanese: 環境のために、私たちはもっとエネルギーを大切に使うべきだ。
examples.english: For the sake of the environment, we should use energy more carefully.

examples.japanese: 病院の中では、大きな声で話すべきではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't talk loudly inside a hospital.

meaning: nothing is as ... as; there's no ... like
structure: Noun + ほど + i-Adj / na-Adj + な + Noun + はない
usage: Says X is the most ... of all, usually from personal experience or feeling. Also 〜くらい〜はない.

examples.japanese: 仕事の後に飲む冷たいビールほどおいしいものはない。
examples.english: Nothing tastes as good as an ice-cold beer after work.

examples.japanese: この町で、あの店ほど安くておいしいラーメン屋はない。
examples.english: There's no ramen shop in this town as cheap and tasty as that one.

examples.japanese: 健康ほど大切なものはないと、病気になって気づいた。
examples.english: When I got sick, I realized that nothing is as important as good health.

meaning: have no choice but to; can only
structure: Verb-dict + しかない
usage: No other option exists, so the speaker accepts this one. Differs from Noun + しか〜ない ('only'). Formal N2 equivalent: 〜ほかない.

examples.japanese: 終電に乗り遅れたから、タクシーで帰るしかない。
examples.english: I missed the last train, so I have no choice but to take a taxi home.

examples.japanese: 誰も手伝ってくれないなら、一人でやるしかない。
examples.english: If nobody will help me, I'll just have to do it myself.

examples.japanese: ここまで来たら、もう最後まで頑張るしかないね。
examples.english: Now that we've come this far, all we can do is give it our all to the end.

meaning: even (an extreme case)
structure: Noun + まで / Noun + にまで
usage: Adds an extreme item on top of others, often with surprise or dismay. Compare 〜さえ, which picks out one extreme example on its own.

examples.japanese: 最近は、小学生までスマホを持っている。
examples.english: These days even elementary school kids have smartphones.

examples.japanese: 親友にまでうそをつかれて、とてもショックだった。
examples.english: I was really shocked that even my best friend lied to me.

examples.japanese: 雨だけでなく、風まで強くなってきた。
examples.english: It's not just the rain; now even the wind is getting stronger.

meaning: almost; nearly (but didn't)
structure: Verb-dict + ところだった
usage: Something (usually bad) came very close to happening but didn't. Often with もう少しで, 危うく or a 〜たら clause. Compare 〜そうになった.

examples.japanese: 考え事をしていて、もう少しで車にひかれるところだった。
examples.english: I was lost in thought and nearly got hit by a car.

examples.japanese: 目覚ましが鳴らなくて、危うく飛行機に乗り遅れるところだった。
examples.english: My alarm didn't go off, and I very nearly missed my flight.

examples.japanese: 君が教えてくれなかったら、大事な書類を出し忘れるところだったよ。
examples.english: If you hadn't reminded me, I would have forgotten to hand in the important documents.

meaning: just because (... doesn't mean); simply because
structure: Sentence + からといって
usage: Denies that a reason automatically leads to a conclusion. Usually followed by a negative such as 〜わけではない or 〜とは限らない. Casual: 〜からって.

examples.japanese: 日本人だからといって、みんなが敬語を正しく使えるわけではない。
examples.english: Just because someone is Japanese doesn't mean they can use keigo correctly.

examples.japanese: 忙しいからといって、朝ご飯を食べないのは体によくない。
examples.english: Skipping breakfast just because you're busy isn't good for you.

examples.japanese: 一回負けたからといって、あきらめる必要はない。
examples.english: There's no need to give up just because you lost once.

meaning: as; in the way that; exactly as
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / Noun + の + とおりに / Noun + どおりに
usage: Doing something exactly like a model, instruction or prediction. Directly after a noun it becomes どおり (予定どおり, 思いどおり). に is often dropped. そのとおりだ = 'exactly'.

examples.japanese: 説明書に書いてあるとおりに組み立てたのに、うまく動かない。
examples.english: I put it together exactly as the manual says, but it doesn't work properly.

examples.japanese: 先生が言ったとおり、試験には去年と似た問題が出た。
examples.english: Just as the teacher said, questions similar to last year's came up on the exam.

examples.japanese: 工事は予定どおりに進んでいる。
examples.english: The construction is going according to schedule.

meaning: things like; the likes of (dismissive or humble); how ...! (surprise)
structure: Noun + なんか / Noun + なんて / Sentence + なんて
usage: Casual version of など with a dismissive, humble or surprised tone. なんか also softens suggestions (お茶なんかどう？). Sentence + なんて shows surprise or disbelief.

examples.japanese: 私なんか、まだまだ初心者です。
examples.english: Someone like me is still just a beginner.

examples.japanese: 幽霊なんて、いるわけがないよ。
examples.english: Ghosts? There's no way they exist.

examples.japanese: あの二人が結婚するなんて、びっくりした。
examples.english: Those two are getting married? I was so surprised!
